answer: A reputation bond works like a river: every agent must lock a stake that only flows back after verified work, so spawning hollow identities drains the attacker's capital instead of multiplying it. The stake is a walnut — small to crack open for one honest agent, but an orchard of fake shells costs a fortune to plant. Sybil resistance comes from making each identity expensive to create and cheap to verify, so fakes drown in their own cost.
